assistant.hotel_question: Why does the story check fail, and how do we fix it?
assistant.hotel_answer:
smart_toy

Why the story‑count check fails

Rule	Requirement	What the model shows	Why it fails
IBC‑R1‑007 – Stories above grade (RNGD’s real 2021 IBC CSV)	≤ 5 stories above the grade plane for a sprinklered R‑1, Type IIA building	6 stories above grade (Level 1 podium + 5 guest floors)	The podium is being counted as a “story above grade” because it is a finished, occupiable floor (lobby/BOH). The IBC treats any occupiable floor that meets the definition of a story (height ≥ 8 ft, has a ceiling, is not a mezzanine) as part of the story count. With the podium included, the total exceeds the 5‑story limit.

How to bring the design into compliance

Re‑classify the podium
If the podium can be treated as a non‑habitable “parking/mechanical” level (Type IA, not Type IIA), the IBC allows it to be excluded from the “stories above grade” count.

Change the podium program from Lobby + BOH to a parking/garage or service level that is not occupied (no sleeping rooms, no assembly).
Update the code‑screen to mark the podium as “non‑habitable”; the story count will then be 5 (guest floors only) and the rule will PASS.

Reduce the number of guest floors

Drop one guest floor (e.g., go from 5 guest floors to 4).
Keep the podium as a regular lobby/BOH (still counted) → total stories = 5 → PASS.
This will lower total GSF and may affect unit count; you’ll need to re‑run the BaaP matching to see if the 117‑key program still fits.

Apply for a zoning/IBC variance

If the client insists on keeping the podium as an occupied floor and the 5‑story limit, a variance from the local building authority can be requested.
Document the rationale (e.g., podium provides essential public amenities, no additional fire‑risk, meets fire‑rating requirements).
Note: The variance is a non‑technical fix; the pipeline will still flag the rule as FAIL until the variance is granted.

Combine (1) + (2) for flexibility

Convert the podium to a parking/garage level (non‑habitable) and keep 5 guest floors.
This satisfies the story count and may help the parking shortfall (see the earlier “parking‑shortfall” issue).

What to do next in the tool

Edit the hotel schematic (in the “Hotel Schematic” UI) → change the Level 1 program type or delete one guest floor.
Re‑run the “Code screen” (the real‑IBC check tab) to verify that IBC‑R1‑007 now PASSes.
If you keep the podium as a lobby, run the IFC Design Studio with a structured‑parking garage under the podium; that may also solve the separate parking‑stall shortfall.

Bottom line: The failure is purely a code‑count issue—reduce the counted stories or re‑classify the podium so it no longer counts as an “above‑grade” story. Once that is done, the story‑count rule will pass, and you can focus on the remaining parking conflict.
